I'd refuse this one. The brief shows a near-total operator setup: 22 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation bought 835 SOL, with a top-5 buyer share of 99.9%, a sell-to-buy ratio near zero, and a launch bot present. The bundle share and top-3 share are both 1.0. This is the profile of a coin where a single operator holds the float, and the desk would be buying into an exit it can't see coming.

Current sell-side pressure is thin (8.96 SOL sold in the last 15 minutes against 12.28 bought), but that tells us little when the largest holders haven't sold yet. Pool depth of ~935 SOL is adequate for a $20 ticket, so liquidity isn't the blocker. The problem is who else is holding.

Refuse at any size. No stop or hold window is needed because there is no entry. The name ("United States Oil Supply") is a creator-chosen label and carries no information about the coin's fundamentals.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying USOS now is thin, and I don't think it clears the bar.

What the brief does show: the coin is alive, the pool holds about 935 SOL, price is up 5% over 30 minutes and roughly flat off its high, and the last 15 minutes brought 40 buyers and net inflow of 3.3 SOL. Those are the only signs of live demand.

Against that, the structure is the problem. The bundle share is 100%, the top 5 buyers hold 99.9% of early purchases, and 835 SOL came in from 22 wallets in the first two minutes after graduation. That is an operator-backed launch, and the sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0008 says almost nobody sold early, which reads as concentrated holding, not broad conviction. The recent 15-minute sell side (9 SOL, 31 sellers) is also heavier than the buy side in count, and the operator wallets have the entire float to exit into whenever they choose.

The name is a current-events hook ("United States Oil Supply"), which may draw attention, but nothing in the brief shows that attention is sustained or organic.

I see no case here that real demand will still be present in 30 to 60 minutes. I'd recommend skipping this coin.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is insider distribution. The curve data is a textbook operator setup: bundle_share 1.0, top3_share 1.0, and top5 buyers holding 99.9% of the first two minutes' 835 SOL, with only 22 non-agent buyers. Those early holders can sell into any retail demand at will, and the sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0008 shows almost no organic selling pressure has ever been absorbed, so there is no proven floor. The last 15 minutes show a 0.7% return on $2,502 volume with net flow of only 3.3 SOL, so the 30-minute return of 5.25% is thin and fragile. Against round-trip fees of 1.4-5.1% on a $20 ticket, even a modest insider sell-off erases the entire edge. Skip.
